original_value: It is difficult to recover the residual heat from flue gas when supercritical carbon dioxide (S-CO2) cycle is used for a coal fired power plant, due to the higher CO2 temperature in tail flue and the limited air temperature in air preheater. The combined cycle is helpful for residual heat recovery. Thus, it is important to build an efficient bottom cycle. In this paper, we proposed a novel exergy destruction control strategy during residual heat recovery to equal and minimize the exergy destruction for different bottom cycles. Five bottom cycles are analyzed to identify their differences in thermal efficiencies (ηth,b), and the CO2 temperature entering the bottom cycle heater (T4b) etc. We show that the exergy destruction can be minimized by a suitable pinch temperature between flue gas and CO2 in the heater via adjusting T4b. Among the five bottom cycles, either the recompression cycle (RC) or the partial cooling cycle (PACC) exhibits good performance. The power generation efficiency is 47.04% when the vapor parameters of CO2 are 620/30 MPa, with the double-reheating-recompression cycle as the top cycle, and RC as the bottom cycle. Such efficiency is higher than that of the supercritical water cycle power plant.

result.paraphrase: Recovering residual heat from flue gas is challenging in coal-fired power plants using a supercritical carbon dioxide (S-CO2) cycle because the CO2 temperature in the tail flue is relatively high and the air temperature available in the air preheater is limited. A combined cycle can improve residual heat recovery, so an efficient bottom cycle is crucial. In this paper, we propose a new exergy-destruction control strategy for residual heat recovery that equalizes and minimizes exergy destruction across different bottom cycles. Five bottom cycles are examined to compare thermal efficiency (ηth,b), the CO2 inlet temperature to the bottom-cycle heater (T4b), and related differences. The results show that exergy destruction can be reduced by selecting an appropriate pinch temperature between the flue gas and CO2 in the heater through adjustment of T4b. Of the five bottom cycles, the recompression cycle (RC) and the partial cooling cycle (PACC) perform well. When the CO2 vapor parameters are 620/30 MPa, the top cycle is the double-reheating-recompression cycle, and RC is used as the bottom cycle, the power-generation efficiency reaches 47.04%. This efficiency is higher than that of a supercritical water cycle power plant.
